subject.title: [Feature]: Add talk.realtime.providers.<id>.baseUrl for OpenAI Realtime-compatible providers

question: Should OpenClaw support non-OpenAI Realtime-compatible endpoints through a generic Talk provider capability/relay contract, or should it add a narrowly scoped direct-endpoint mode to the existing OpenAI provider?
rationale: This choice sets a long-lived configuration and credential-exposure contract across Talk clients and realtime providers; source-level repair cannot safely choose the supported auth boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design a relay/provider capability
options.body: Define provider-owned endpoint and authentication capabilities that preserve server-side credential handling, then implement supported providers against that contract.

options.title: Add a narrow OpenAI-compatible mode
options.body: Permit only documented compatible endpoints after proving their session protocol and direct-key browser exposure are safe and adding explicit upgrade and security tests.

options.title: Defer direct compatibility support
options.body: Keep the current OpenAI-specific path and route provider-specific realtime integrations through plugins or a future relay design.

recommendation.title: Design a relay/provider capability
recommendation.body: Define provider-owned endpoint and authentication capabilities that preserve server-side credential handling, then implement supported providers against that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a product and credential-boundary decision spanning core Talk and provider architecture.
